analysis.title: FOMC Signals / Alphabet & Samsung / ECB Ahead / Trade Ideas / TOPIX
key_insights: FOMC held rates unchanged in a 10-2 vote. Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favour of a 25bp hike. Chair Warsh gave no clear signal on a December hike.

UBS Macro Sales Trading calls the FOMC messaging strange. Warsh pointed to more data even though the data since September would at minimum support a hawkish tone, and the discussion focused mainly on price stability. The statement described activity as expanding at a strong pace in September.

Starting fall 2027 the FOMC keeps eight meetings but one has no rate decision or statement (two meetings in 2028). The swap market read this as one fewer opportunity to hike. Treasuries ended mixed with a twist-steepening curve, front end outperforming and the long end lagging.

Alphabet Q3 Search growth was 11.8% vs 14-14.5% buyside and 15% Street expectations. YouTube grew 11% vs a 12% bogey and operating income was $41bn vs $44-45bn expected. The stock fell 9% after hours and Nasdaq futures fell as much as 1%. The desk says AI cannibalization of Search is back in focus.
Microsoft rose 2.7% after hours on Azure growth of 48% vs 45.2% expected. Capex of $39.37bn was below the $46.54bn expected.

Oracle's CFO reportedly forecast positive free cash flow in H2 fiscal 2028 and above $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capital spending declines. Oracle rose 10.7% overnight. The desk notes this is not good news for AI upstream names.

Samsung Electronics Q3 revenue of KRW195.3trn was 7% below UBS and 3% below consensus. Operating profit of KRW107.4trn missed UBS by 9% and was broadly in line with consensus. Net income missed consensus by 14%. Shares fell 2.5% after the release. HBM4 ramp and server SSD demand support the memory thesis, and 2026 shareholder returns of KRW90-110trn exceeded expectations.

Zain Nizami (Cash Equity Voice Trading) recommends fading long delta and not chasing Tech. He sees the Tech flow pickup as an unwind of hedging, favours defensives with selective broadening, and says broadening depends on oil moving lower.
UBS European Economics expects the ECB to hold the depo rate at 2.5% on Thursday, in line with consensus, and sees hikes in December 2026 and March 2027.

UBS FX Strategy targets EURUSD at 1.10 by Q1 2027 and 1.07 by Q2, citing French fiscal concerns, energy exposure and US rates. FX Sales suggests 6m EURUSD digital downside or a cheaper worst-of EUR basket.

The TOPIX annual rebalance on Thursday's close has estimated passive turnover of $59.0bn (revised from $63.3bn), still a record. Kioxia is the largest buy at $5.13bn (1.08 days ADV) and Mitsubishi the largest sell at -$1.62bn.
Equity Sales suggests buying TOPIX Banks via call spreads after a roughly 12% correction driven by lower yields, positioning unwind and AI-financing concerns.
ServiceNow fell 15% vs about 9.7% implied volatility after cRPO guidance disappointed. Q3 cRPO rose 19.5% y/y to $13.65bn and Q4 guidance of 18.9% was below 19.5% consensus.
Microsoft fiscal Q1 revenue was $92.28bn vs $90.6bn expected, EPS $4.92 vs $4.71, and operating margin 49.8% vs 48.6%.

Korea's October business sentiment index rose 5.1 points to 104.2, the highest since August 2022. UBS FX Strategy favours AUDNZD topside, and the Bank of Thailand held at 1% with UBS expecting a 25bp hike in Q4 2027.
UBS RESFER 47s offer about 5.5% yield and about 22bp over interpolated OATs. Warsh said some Fed task forces will miss the year-end deadline and the balance sheet task force reports early in Q1.

Microsoft fiscal Q1 (reported 10/28 after close): revenue $92.28bn vs $90.6bn expected. EPS $4.92 vs $4.71 expected. Azure growth 48% vs 45.2% expected. Gross margin 67.8% vs 67.2%. Operating income $45.9bn vs $44.07bn. Capex $39.37bn vs $46.54bn expected.
ServiceNow Q3 (reported): cRPO $13.65bn, up 19.5% y/y. The sequential beat of about 100bp was below a 150-200bp bogey. Q4 cRPO growth guidance 18.9% vs consensus 19.5%.

Samsung Electronics Q3 (reported): revenue KRW195.3trn, 7% below UBS and 3% below consensus. Operating profit KRW107.4trn, 9% below UBS and broadly in line with consensus. Net income 14% below consensus, partly due to KRW9.5trn net finance expenses. 2026 capex is planned at KRW84.4trn.
Oracle: CFO reportedly forecast free cash flow turning positive in H2 fiscal 2028 and topping $30bn in fiscal 2029, when capital spending declines.
